findings.what: The naming commit makes the public audit reject valid current C expressions as opaque Base85/Z85. Examples are MoveDataToVRAM(&gCameraRowUploadWords[camera][first_count], ...), InitializeLevelZeroFixedItems(&gObjectTable[bank][28]) and !IsSpriteSlotNonReclaimable(entity->primary_shadow). The bounded expression exemption does not recognize these unary/address/member-expression shapes; the entropy scan then treats their long renamed identifiers plus punctuation as encoded payload. The real public/history gate fails despite the synthetic suite passing. These are directly inspected source expressions, not private payloads.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend only the bounded, atom-checked source-expression recognizer to cover the demonstrated valid expression shapes (preserving all ROM/numeric/media and opaque-atom checks), add regression fixtures for each and their encoded-payload negative controls, and run the public-history gate on the corrected prepared inputs. Merely adding whitespace to HEAD is insufficient because the rejected naming commit remains in history.

findings.what: The requested history audit also fails on legitimate historical public source. In tree 004896a4e025, include/title_calls.h is a 793-byte K&R declaration header whose bytes at offset 256 begin SEGAAndIntroVideoRoutine, so the four-byte raw[256:260] == b'SEGA' heuristic declares it an embedded Genesis ROM. A historical arithmetic/comment expression in src/z80/initial_bootstrap.s also crosses the opaque Base64 threshold. These inherited false positives prevent a clean all-history result even after the four current C-expression cases are corrected.
findings.suggested_fix: Strengthen Genesis payload recognition with actual bounded cartridge/header structure rather than a four-character coincidence inside printable source; add the historical header as a source-safe regression alongside synthetic real-ROM negative fixtures. Identify and recognize the historical ordinary Z80 expression through a narrow grammar/structured shape, not a path/file/history blanket exemption. Preserve adversarial opaque-string coverage and rerun the full-history gate after the fix.
